blocks.h2: Signs Your McHenry Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: The calls we take most in McHenry County:

tiles.body: Mineral sediment on the bottom of the tank traps water that boils underneath it. It's the classic hard-water sound.
A thick layer of sediment takes up room in the tank, or an electric element has burned out under it.
Iron from the water supply, a spent anode rod or a tank that's starting to rust.

tiles.h3: A Leak at the Drain Valve or Base
tiles.body: Sediment can keep the drain valve from sealing. A leak from the tank itself means replacement.

blocks.h2: Why Water Heaters Struggle in McHenry
blocks.intro: McHenry County gets its water from underground aquifers, not Lake Michigan. That water is great to have, but it's hard on water heaters.

items.body: Groundwater here tends to be hard. As the heater warms the water, minerals drop out and settle on the bottom of the tank. The burner then has to heat through a layer of scale, which wastes energy and stresses the tank.

Some water systems in the area carry iron. Outside city limits, residents of unincorporated Eastwood Manor, on a small private water system, reported orange water and sediment ruining water heaters until Aqua Illinois added iron filtration in 2025.
About 4 in 10 McHenry homes went up between 1990 and 2009. Heaters from the first or second round in those homes are often near the end.
Many homes here have a softener. If it's out of salt or not regenerating, scale returns quickly. We check it during water heater calls.

bodies: We repair every type of home water heater in McHenry County: gas and electric tanks, power-vent and high-efficiency models and tankless units. We diagnose first and recommend second.

Read us the label on the side of the tank when you call. The fuel, the size and the manufacture date tell us a lot about whether repair makes sense. If it's time for a new heater, see [water heater installation](/mchenry/water-heater-installation).
In McHenry County, a yearly flush isn't an extra. Hard water leaves sediment in every tank, and flushing it out before it hardens is the single best thing you can do for your heater's life.

A maintenance visit includes the flush, a test of the relief valve, an anode rod check and a look at the burner or elements and the vent. Tankless units get descaled. If you have a softener or a [filtration system](/mchenry/water-filtration-systems), we'll make sure it's doing its job.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: Is McHenry's hard water tough on my water heater?
items.preview: Yes. Minerals settle in the tank and shorten its life.
items.answer: It can be. Groundwater in McHenry County tends to be hard, and some areas carry iron. Those minerals settle in the tank as sediment, so the heater works harder and wears out sooner. Yearly flushing and a working softener help.

items.q: Why is my water heater making popping noises?
items.preview: Sediment on the bottom of the tank.
items.answer: Water trapped under sediment on the tank bottom boils and pops as the burner heats it. A flush can help if the sediment hasn't hardened. If it has, the tank may be near the end.

items.q: Why is my hot water orange but my cold water isn't?
items.preview: Usually the anode rod or tank corrosion. Sometimes iron collecting in the tank.
items.answer: If only the hot side is orange, the problem is usually in the heater: a spent anode rod, rust inside the tank or iron sediment collecting in the bottom. If both sides are orange, the iron is coming from your water supply.

items.q: How long do water heaters last in McHenry County?
items.preview: Usually about 8 to 12 years. Hard water can push that to the low end.
items.answer: Tank heaters usually last somewhere around 8 to 12 years. Without regular flushing, hard water tends to push that toward the low end.
